channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Beyond "Biomedical-Plus": Reclaiming the biopsychosocial model in musculoskeletal physiotherapy.
item.description: The biopsychosocial (BPS) model is often reduced to "biomedical-plus" in MSK physiotherapy. This article argues for a more authentic BPS application through professional Confidence, role Clarity, and Compassionate communication.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Combined Biopsychosocial Interventions for Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found combined biopsychosocial interventions significantly reduce pain and functional disability in adults with chronic low back pain (≥12 weeks) compared to usual care or unimodal interventions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative efficacy of different joint mobilization techniques in shoulder adhesive capsulitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared different non-thrust joint mobilization techniques for shoulder adhesive capsulitis, reinforcing their fundamental role in conservative physical therapy management.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Cost-effectiveness of stratified physiotherapy integrated with digital health versus usual physiotherapy for neck and/or shoulder pain: results of a cluster randomised clinical trial.
item.description: A cluster randomized clinical trial found that a Stratified Blended Physiotherapy Approach (SBPA), integrating prognostic risk stratification with digital health, was cost-effective compared to usual physiotherapy for 136 patients with neck and/or shoulder pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of an individualised swimming and education programme for chronic low back pain (EduSwim): a randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An individualized swimming and education program, delivered via telehealth, significantly improved disability in adults with chronic non-specific low back pain at 8 weeks compared to education alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual Reality-assisted Physiotherapeutic Training for Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 RCTs found that virtual reality-assisted physiotherapy significantly improved pain (SMD = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.14-0.65), physical function (SMD = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.05-0.70), and balance (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.16-0.72) in patients with knee osteoarthritis compared to traditional rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association of combined physical and cognitive rehabilitation with post-stroke dementia: a U.S. multicenter retrospective cohort study.
item.description: A U.S. multicenter retrospective cohort study of 958 propensity score-matched stroke patients (≥55 years) with mild cognitive impairment found that combined physical and cognitive rehabilitation was associated with a significantly reduced risk of post-stroke dementia (HR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.44-0.78, P < 0.001) compared to physical rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The RESOLVE Trial: A Stepped-Wedge, Cluster-Randomized Clinical Trial Evaluating the Effects of Clinical Practice Guidelines and Psychologically Informed Physical Therapy on Low Back Pain Outcomes in Service Members and Veterans.
item.description: A stepped-wedge, cluster-randomized trial showed that implementing clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) alongside psychologically informed physical therapy (PIPT) significantly reduced low back pain-related disability and pain in military and veteran health care settings.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Outpatient rehabilitation can prevent suicide after acquired brain injury.
item.description: A registry study (n=591 treated patients, n=2,932 controls) suggests that outpatient rehabilitation may prevent suicide after acquired brain injury, with a higher suicide frequency found in general population post-stroke and TBI.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Optimised oxygenation improves functional capacity during ...
item.description: An RCT demonstrated that optimized oxygenation improved functional capacity during daily activities in patients with COPD on long-term oxygen therapy.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: A systematic review of current evidence on clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques in sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
item.description: This systematic review aims to evaluate the clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques for sacroiliac joint dysfunction (SIJD), with studies published between January 2021 and December 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-term benefits of ultrasound-guided percutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for chronic lateral elbow pain: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized, double-blinded, sham-controlled trial with 49 participants found that ultrasound-guided percutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, combined with exercise, provided mid- and long-term benefits for chronic lateral elbow pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Content validity, reliability, and agreement between in-person and video-call assessments of the modified bradykinesia rating scale (MBRS).
item.description: The Modified Bradykinesia Rating Scale (MBRS) demonstrated adequate content validity, excellent test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.94-0.97) and inter-rater reliability (ICC = 0.82-0.97), and good agreement between in-person and video-call assessments in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: In adult patients with brainstem strokes, does dysphagia rehabilitation improve health-related outcomes compared to usual care for inpatients? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies (443 participants) concluded that dysphagia rehabilitation, including traditional swallowing therapy and device inclusion, is effective for improving swallow function in inpatients with brainstem stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Multimodal Assessment of Gastric Motility, reflux risk, and Clinical Efficacy: Intermittent Oro-Esophageal versus Nasogastric Tube Feeding for Post-Stroke Dysphagia in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-center RCT with 54 post-stroke dysphagia patients found that intermittent oro-esophageal tube feeding (IOE) was superior to nasogastric tube feeding (NG) for reducing gastric retention volume (40.5 ± 25.3 ml vs. 79.2 ± 36.1 ml, p < 0.001) and reflux risk (4.2% vs. 20.8%, p = 0.02) after 14 days, while supporting swallowing recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploring equity in telehealth interventions in physiotherapy: A meta-epidemiological study.
item.description: A meta-epidemiological study (n=94 telehealth equity trials) assessed equity in physiotherapy telehealth interventions using the PROGRESS Plus framework, identifying gaps in reaching vulnerable populations.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of resistance-band shoulder exercise on pain, range of motion, and functional disability in diabetic adults with adhesive capsulitis: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A pilot randomized controlled trial with 28 diabetic adults with adhesive capsulitis suggests that resistance-band shoulder exercises may improve pain, range of motion, and functional disability, though further larger studies are needed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Spine-related leg pain: Definitions, etiology, clinical presentation, and management.
item.description: Spine-related leg pain (SRLP) is a common and debilitating condition. This review clarifies SRLP terminology, distinguishing radiculopathy, radicular pain, and somatic referred pain, aiming to reduce diagnostic uncertainty and improve management.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital Addiction and Body Balance: An Investigation of Postural Stability in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
item.description: This cross-sectional study (n=74) found young adults with smartphone addiction exhibited impaired postural stability, particularly under attention-demanding tasks, highlighting the impact of digital device use on balance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Assessment and Management Practices for Post-Stroke Shoulder Pain Among Rehabilitation Professionals in Vietnam: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
item.description: A cross-sectional survey in Vietnam investigated rehabilitation professionals' practices for post-stroke shoulder pain, identifying potential gaps between evidence and clinical application, particularly in lower- and middle-income countries.
item.author: PubMed
